Since the settlement, the Petitioner raised pucca structures at huge costs and possessed the same as a non-agricultural tenant on payment of yearly rent by running business in part of it and letting out the other part to tenants on monthly rental.

Subsequently, a proceeding was started, being No.2734 of 1961 under Section 49 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 for revision at the instance of the local Tahsildar on the grounds that the disputed land is a part of Taha-Bazar and khas land of the Ex-rent receiver: The petitioner contested the proceeding by submitting his written objections and stating, amongst other that the land in question was not the. Khas land of the Ex. land receiver. The Assistant Settlement Officer has allowed the objections of the Petitioner by his order dated 21.10.1961. But the Opposite Party preferred a Revisional application on the grounds that the disputed plot was within the ambit and periphery of the Ananda Bazar, whereupon the settlement officer directed a local enquiry by the Charge officer. Comilla and the charge officer submitted a report stating that the bulk area of Gagat Bazar would not be taken to be within the periphery of Fiat except two small plots. Viz 3725 and 3543, which might he kept under acquisition and the rest may by recorded in the names of the possessors:. The plot numbers 3170, 3167, 3157, 3156, 3145, 3144, 3232, 3134, 3139, 3136 and 3130 might be taken within the periphery of flat and recorded in the name of the Collector and the remaining plots might he recorded in the names of the .possessors and the Compensation Assessment Roll he corrected accordingly.

But a notice was served upon them acquiring the property against which the Petitioners tiled the Miscellaneous Case No. 12 of 1962 which was dismissed summarily on 14.1.1963. The Petitioners then preferred the Special Appeal No. 30 of 1964 in the Court of the Special Judge which was also dismissed on analogous hearing.

Upon an objection filed by the opposite party, under Section 49 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, a case being No.2731 of 1961 was started and the Assistant Settlement Officer by his order dated 21.10.1961 upheld the records. But the Settlement Officer served a notice upon the Petitioners under Section 49 and 50 of the Act on 18.8.1962 in a Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 1962 where the record was cancelled upon summary rejection of the Petitioner's objection and the learned Special Judge has also been pleased to dismiss the Special Appeal No. 70 of 1963 preferred by the Petitioners by his common judgment dated 31.12.1965.

 of the Learned Advocates for the respective parties and on 25.5.2004, Mr. Harendra Nath Nandy the Learned Advocate, appeared representing the Petitioners, who entered appearance in all the Rules for the Petitioners by filing a Vokalatnama as back as on 6.4.2000 apparent from the office note dated 6.4.2000 and thus the matters have been fixed for hearing and for delivery of judgment on 23.6.2004.  Plot No.1674 was recorded in the names of the persons who were ex-rent receivers and the rent-receiving interests have been acquired by the Province Of East Pakistan by the Notification dated 2nd April. 1956 and the property has vested in the province of East Pakistan free from encumbrances under Section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (2nd Amendment) Ordinance, 1960 (East Pakistan Ordinance No. XII of 1960). 

 In the C.S. Nos.395 and 369 one Radhika Mohan Chowdhury and others were the ex. Rent-receivers under Touzi No.203 in the Pargana "Shatrakhandai" of the Comilla Collectorate. There is no record in the office to show whether these ex. Rent-receivers were Sebait of any Debottar Estate. 

 The land stands recorded in Collector's Khatian No. 1 Under the provisions of the Ordinance No. XII of 1960, lands within the flat-I3atar are non-retainable properties by the Ex-rent receivers, cultivating raiyat or non-agricultural tenants. 

 It is not a fact that the P.R.R. Khatians in respect of alleged Plot numbers were opened in  the names of the Petitioners. One Khatians being No. 527 was opened in the names of the Petitioners in respect of some Plots and that was fraudulently recorded and it was subsequently cancelled by the Settlement Officer, Comilla in proceedings under Section 49 of the Act in the Miscellaneous Cases mentioned by the petitioners. The Rent-Roll, prepared in their names were also cancelled subsequently. No rent was realised from the Petitioners on the basis of that fictitious P.R.R. 

 8. In the Affidavit-in-reply, the Petitioners stated that it was not a fact that the C.S. Plot  No.1674 was acquired by the Opposite Party on 2.4.1956 as non-retainable khan land of the Ex-rent receivers and that Radhika Mohan Chowdhury was a Sebait of Sree Sree Nittayananda Mohaprovu and Sree Sree Radha Govinda Bigraha. The suit land is not covered by the Bazar and the Petitioners are not unauthorized occupants and that the Miscellaneous Cases were dismissed summarily'. 

 While the Section 3 of the Act provided general provisions for acquisition of all rent- receiving interests by the Provincial Government wiping out the rent-receiving intermediary interests completely the Section 20 made an exception to the general provision providing a list of land which the rent-receivers cultivating raiyats cultivating under raiyats and non-agricultural tenants may retain in their possession as khan land. Sub-section 2(a) of Section 20 is again an exception to the exception provided by Section 20. This Sub-Section 2(a) to Section 20 provides that "Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force or in any instrument or in any judgment or decree or order of any Court lands of the classes referred to in the clauses (a) and (h) of sub-section (2) do not include and shall be deemed never to have included — 

 In the case of Jihendra Kishore Roy Chowdhury Vs. the Province of East Pakistan. reported in 9 DI.R(SC) 21, it was held that a Mutwalli or a Sebait is a rent-receiver within the meaning of clause (23) of section 2 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 1950. 

 This case arose out of the Notification No.4839- L.R. issued on 2nd April, 1956 under  sub-section (1) to Section 3 of the Act acquiring of the interests of certain rent-receivers, which was decided by a Full Bench or the then High Court at Dhaka including his Lordship. the Chief Justice Amin Ahmed and reported in 8 DER 457 (The Chief' Justice took pride of its authorship and presented a copy of the printed judgment to Mr. Justice Douglas. while his Lordship was visiting the United States. see "A peep into the past," by Former Chief Justice Amin Ahmed. Page-61). It was held in this case that the Notification was applicable to a Mutwalli or Sebait, thereby divesting them from their interests in the land which whether they vested in the Almighty or a Deity or for the purpose of the Act in the Mutwalli or the Sebait are from the date of the Notification transferred absolutely to the Provincial Government and as per the decision given in the case of Khondakar Ali Afzal Vs. the Province of East Pakistan reported in 18 DLR184, the outgoing Mutwalli or Sebait becomes entitled to compensation as provided in the Act.

Plot No. 1674 under the C.S. Khatian No.395/369 and there is no record in the office of the Collactorate. Comilla to show whether these ex.
